<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead" summary="Fix office role authorization">
Fix accepted CRITICAL security issue f7ee0171-73e9-4df7-a71d-ae9e0f926a5f in /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm: /schedule* and /timesheets* (and any other office-only surfaces) have NO owner/admin role check — any authenticated cleaner can reschedule/price-change/cancel/delete jobs, create plans, and view/export the whole account's payroll. /audit already gates correctly (owner-only via Accounts.get_user_role) — use it as the reference pattern.

MCP note: on "No session_id available" add explicit session_id "b82dc084-1093-4624-b490-31c68a31a4a8"; if MCP hangs >2 min, message me and keep coding.

Implement a shared office-authorization on_mount hook (e.g. CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole in lib/cleaner_crm_web/, checking Accounts.get_user_role(scope, user, active_account) in [:owner, :admin], redirecting others to /field with an error flash) and apply it to the office LiveViews: ScheduleLive.* (Index/PlanLive/JobLive/CleanerLive/AvailabilityLive), TimesheetLive, QualityLive.* (Review/Scorecards/Templates), ReminderLive, InvoiceLive.*, ClientLive.*, QuoteLive.*, AuditLive (keep its stricter owner-only check if present). Cleaners keep: /field*, /users/settings. Also gate the TimesheetExportController (CSV) the same way. Sweep the router's authenticated live_session and decide per-route; the cleaner persona must never see office data. IMPORTANT: the QA seed owner (qa-owner@cleanercrm.test) must retain full access — verify Accounts.get_user_role returns :owner for account creators; the seeded cleaner (qa-cleaner) is a plain member.

Existing tests/specs drive office surfaces as the OWNER (shared givens log in the owner) — they must stay green; specs driving cleaner access to /field must stay green (838/841/842/844/845). Run: MIX_ENV=test mix compile clean, FULL mix spex (100/100 expected) and mix test (160+/0), mix format. Some spex log in as cleaner for field surfaces — if any office-surface spec logged in as a cleaner and breaks, examine whether the spec used the sanctioned owner path; fix the TEST DATA/setup only if it contradicts the security model, and tell me which.

NO dev compile/server restart — the QA server is a detached release; say "NEEDS RELEASE REBUILD" in your report and I'll do it. resolve_issue f7ee0171-73e9-4df7-a71d-ae9e0f926a5f when green. Final response: files, spex/test counts, notes. Under 150 words.
</teammate-message>

- codemyspec:next: Find and start the next requirement task in one gesture. Use after each completed task as your single onboarding instruction.
- codemyspec:product: Product management — guided story interview, review, and Three Amigos sessions. Use when defining what to build, refining requirements, reviewing story quality, or running an Example Mapping session on a story.
- codemyspec:qa: QA testing and issue management — full app QA, per-story QA, integration planning, issue triage, and fixes.
- codemyspec:sync: Sync project components and regenerate architecture views. Use after git pulls, before design sessions, or when views feel stale.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index

      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new

  end

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth do
2	  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes
3	
4	  import Plug.Conn
5	  import Phoenix.Controller
6	
7	  alias CleanerCrm.Users
8	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
9	
10	  # Make the remember me cookie valid for 14 days. This should match
11	  # the session validity setting in UserToken.
12	  @max_cookie_age_in_days 14
13	  @remember_me_cookie "_cleaner_crm_web_user_remember_me"
14	  @remember_me_options [
15	    sign: true,
16	    max_age: @max_cookie_age_in_days * 24 * 60 * 60,
17	    same_site: "Lax"
18	  ]
19	
20	  # How old the session token should be before a new one is issued. When a request is made
21	  # with a session token older than this value, then a new session token will be created
22	  # and the session and remember-me cookies (if set) will be updated with the new token.
23	  # Lowering this value will result in more tokens being created by active users. Increasing
24	  # it will result in less time before a session token expires for a user to get issued a new
25	  # token. This can be set to a value greater than `@max_cookie_age_in_days` to disable
26	  # the reissuing of tokens completely.
27	  @session_reissue_age_in_days 7
28	
29	  @doc """
30	  Logs the user in.
31	
32	  Redirects to the session's `:user_return_to` path
33	  or falls back to the `signed_in_path/1`.
34	  """
35	  def log_in_user(conn, user, params \\ %{}) do
36	    user_return_to = get_session(conn, :user_return_to)
37	
38	    conn
39	    |> create_or_extend_session(user, params)
40	    |> redirect(to: user_return_to || signed_in_path(conn))
41	  end
42	
43	  @doc """
44	  Logs the user out.
45	
46	  It clears all session data for safety. See renew_session.
47	  """
48	  def log_out_user(conn) do
49	    user_token = get_session(conn, :user_token)
50	    user_token && Users.delete_user_session_token(user_token)
51	
52	    if live_socket_id = get_session(conn, :live_socket_id) do
53	      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(live_socket_id, "disconnect", %{})
54	    end
55	
56	    conn
57	    |> renew_session(nil)
58	    |> delete_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, @remember_me_options)
59	    |> redirect(to: ~p"/")
60	  end
61	
62	  @doc """
63	  Authenticates the user by looking into the session and remember me token.
64	
65	  Will reissue the session token if it is older than the configured age.
66	  """
67	  def fetch_current_scope_for_user(conn, _opts) do
68	    with {token, conn} <- ensure_user_token(conn),
69	         {user, token_inserted_at} <- Users.get_user_by_session_token(token) do
70	      conn
71	      |> assign(:current_scope, scope_with_active_account(user))
72	      |> maybe_reissue_user_session_token(user, token_inserted_at)
73	    else
74	      nil -> assign(conn, :current_scope, Scope.for_user(nil))
75	    end
76	  end
77	
78	  defp ensure_user_token(conn) do
79	    if token = get_session(conn, :user_token) do
80	      {token, conn}
81	    else
82	      conn = fetch_cookies(conn, signed: [@remember_me_cookie])
83	
84	      if token = conn.cookies[@remember_me_cookie] do
85	        {token, conn |> put_token_in_session(token) |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)}
86	      else
87	        nil
88	      end
89	    end
90	  end
91	
92	  # Reissue the session token if it is older than the configured reissue age.
93	  defp maybe_reissue_user_session_token(conn, user, token_inserted_at) do
94	    token_age = DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(:second), token_inserted_at, :day)
95	
96	    if token_age >= @session_reissue_age_in_days do
97	      create_or_extend_session(conn, user, %{})
98	    else
99	      conn
100	    end
101	  end
102	
103	  # This function is the one responsible for creating session tokens
104	  # and storing them safely in the session and cookies. It may be called
105	  # either when logging in, during sudo mode, or to renew a session which
106	  # will soon expire.
107	  #
108	  # When the session is created, rather than extended, the renew_session
109	  # function will clear the session to avoid fixation attacks. See the
110	  # renew_session function to customize this behaviour.
111	  defp create_or_extend_session(conn, user, params) do
112	    token = Users.generate_user_session_token(user)
113	    remember_me = get_session(conn, :user_remember_me)
114	
115	    conn
116	    |> renew_session(user)
117	    |> put_token_in_session(token)
118	    |> maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(token, params, remember_me)
119	  end
120	
121	  # Do not renew session if the user is already logged in
122	  # to prevent CSRF errors or data being lost in tabs that are still open
123	  defp renew_session(conn, user) when conn.assigns.current_scope.user.id == user.id do
124	    conn
125	  end
126	
127	  # This function renews the session ID and erases the whole
128	  # session to avoid fixation attacks. If there is any data
129	  # in the session you may want to preserve after log in/log out,
130	  # you must explicitly fetch the session data before clearing
131	  # and then immediately set it after clearing, for example:
132	  #
133	  #     defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
134	  #       delete_csrf_token()
135	  #       preferred_locale = get_session(conn, :preferred_locale)
136	  #
137	  #       conn
138	  #       |> configure_session(renew: true)
139	  #       |> clear_session()
140	  #       |> put_session(:preferred_locale, preferred_locale)
141	  #     end
142	  #
143	  defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
144	    delete_csrf_token()
145	
146	    conn
147	    |> configure_session(renew: true)
148	    |> clear_session()
149	  end
150	
151	  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, %{"remember_me" => "true"}, _),
152	    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)
153	
154	  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, _params, true),
155	    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)
156	
157	  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, _token, _params, _), do: conn
158	
159	  defp write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token) do
160	    conn
161	    |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)
162	    |> put_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, token, @remember_me_options)
163	  end
164	
165	  defp put_token_in_session(conn, token) do
166	    conn
167	    |> put_session(:user_token, token)
168	    |> put_session(:live_socket_id, user_session_topic(token))
169	  end
170	
171	  @doc """
172	  Disconnects existing sockets for the given tokens.
173	  """
174	  def disconnect_sessions(tokens) do
175	    Enum.each(tokens, fn %{token: token} ->
176	      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(user_session_topic(token), "disconnect", %{})
177	    end)
178	  end
179	
180	  defp user_session_topic(token), do: "users_sessions:#{Base.url_encode64(token)}"
181	
182	  @doc """
183	  Handles mounting and authenticating the current_scope in LiveViews.
184	
185	  ## `on_mount` arguments
186	
187	    * `:mount_current_scope` - Assigns current_scope
188	      to socket assigns based on user_token, or nil if
189	      there's no user_token or no matching user.
190	
191	    * `:require_authenticated` - Authenticates the user from the session,
192	      and assigns the current_scope to socket assigns based
193	      on user_token.
194	      Redirects to login page if there's no logged user.
195	
196	  ## Examples
197	
198	  Use the `on_mount` lifecycle macro in LiveViews to mount or authenticate
199	  the `current_scope`:
200	
201	      defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PageLive do
202	        use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view
203	
204	        on_mount {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}
205	        ...
206	      end
207	
208	  Or use the `live_session` of your router to invoke the on_mount callback:
209	
210	      live_session :authenticated, on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
211	        live "/profile", ProfileLive, :index
212	      end
213	  """
214	  def on_mount(:mount_current_scope, _params, session, socket) do
215	    {:cont, mount_current_scope(socket, session)}
216	  end
217	
218	  def on_mount(:require_authenticated, _params, session, socket) do
219	    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)
220	
221	    if socket.assigns.current_scope && socket.assigns.current_scope.user do
222	      {:cont, socket}
223	    else
224	      socket =
225	        socket
226	        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must log in to access this page.")
227	        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")
228	
229	      {:halt, socket}
230	    end
231	  end
232	
233	  def on_mount(:require_sudo_mode, _params, session, socket) do
234	    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)
235	
236	    if Users.sudo_mode?(socket.assigns.current_scope.user, -10) do
237	      {:cont, socket}
238	    else
239	      socket =
240	        socket
241	        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must re-authenticate to access this page.")

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  import Plug.Conn
  import Phoenix.Controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  # Make the remember me cookie valid for 14 days. This should match
  # the session validity setting in UserToken.
  @max_cookie_age_in_days 14
  @remember_me_cookie "_cleaner_crm_web_user_remember_me"
  @remember_me_options [
    sign: true,
    max_age: @max_cookie_age_in_days * 24 * 60 * 60,
    same_site: "Lax"
  ]

  # How old the session token should be before a new one is issued. When a request is made
  # with a session token older than this value, then a new session token will be created
  # and the session and remember-me cookies (if set) will be updated with the new token.
  # Lowering this value will result in more tokens being created by active users. Increasing
  # it will result in less time before a session token expires for a user to get issued a new
  # token. This can be set to a value greater than `@max_cookie_age_in_days` to disable
  # the reissuing of tokens completely.
  @session_reissue_age_in_days 7

  @doc """
  Logs the user in.

  Redirects to the session's `:user_return_to` path
  or falls back to the `signed_in_path/1`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, params \\ %{}) do
    user_return_to = get_session(conn, :user_return_to)

    conn
    |> create_or_extend_session(user, params)
    |> redirect(to: user_return_to || signed_in_path(conn))
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the user out.

  It clears all session data for safety. See renew_session.
  """
  def log_out_user(conn) do
    user_token = get_session(conn, :user_token)
    user_token && Users.delete_user_session_token(user_token)

    if live_socket_id = get_session(conn, :live_socket_id) do
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(live_socket_id, "disconnect", %{})
    end

    conn
    |> renew_session(nil)
    |> delete_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, @remember_me_options)
    |> redirect(to: ~p"/")
  end

  @doc """
  Authenticates the user by looking into the session and remember me token.

  Will reissue the session token if it is older than the configured age.
  """
  def fetch_current_scope_for_user(conn, _opts) do
    with {token, conn} <- ensure_user_token(conn),
         {user, token_inserted_at} <- Users.get_user_by_session_token(token) do
      conn
      |> assign(:current_scope, scope_with_active_account(user))
      |> maybe_reissue_user_session_token(user, token_inserted_at)
    else
      nil -> assign(conn, :current_scope, Scope.for_user(nil))
    end
  end

  defp ensure_user_token(conn) do
    if token = get_session(conn, :user_token) do
      {token, conn}
    else
      conn = fetch_cookies(conn, signed: [@remember_me_cookie])

      if token = conn.cookies[@remember_me_cookie] do
        {token, conn |> put_token_in_session(token) |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)}
      else
        nil
      end
    end
  end

  # Reissue the session token if it is older than the configured reissue age.
  defp maybe_reissue_user_session_token(conn, user, token_inserted_at) do
    token_age = DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(:second), token_inserted_at, :day)

    if token_age >= @session_reissue_age_in_days do
      create_or_extend_session(conn, user, %{})
    else
      conn
    end
  end

  # This function is the one responsible for creating session tokens
  # and storing them safely in the session and cookies. It may be called
  # either when logging in, during sudo mode, or to renew a session which
  # will soon expire.
  #
  # When the session is created, rather than extended, the renew_session
  # function will clear the session to avoid fixation attacks. See the
  # renew_session function to customize this behaviour.
  defp create_or_extend_session(conn, user, params) do
    token = Users.generate_user_session_token(user)
    remember_me = get_session(conn, :user_remember_me)

    conn
    |> renew_session(user)
    |> put_token_in_session(token)
    |> maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(token, params, remember_me)
  end

  # Do not renew session if the user is already logged in
  # to prevent CSRF errors or data being lost in tabs that are still open
  defp renew_session(conn, user) when conn.assigns.current_scope.user.id == user.id do
    conn
  end

  # This function renews the session ID and erases the whole
  # session to avoid fixation attacks. If there is any data
  # in the session you may want to preserve after log in/log out,
  # you must explicitly fetch the session data before clearing
  # and then immediately set it after clearing, for example:
  #
  #     defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
  #       delete_csrf_token()
  #       preferred_locale = get_session(conn, :preferred_locale)
  #
  #       conn
  #       |> configure_session(renew: true)
  #       |> clear_session()
  #       |> put_session(:preferred_locale, preferred_locale)
  #     end
  #
  defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
    delete_csrf_token()

    conn
    |> configure_session(renew: true)
    |> clear_session()
  end

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, %{"remember_me" => "true"}, _),
    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, _params, true),
    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, _token, _params, _), do: conn

  defp write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token) do
    conn
    |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)
    |> put_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, token, @remember_me_options)
  end

  defp put_token_in_session(conn, token) do
    conn
    |> put_session(:user_token, token)
    |> put_session(:live_socket_id, user_session_topic(token))
  end

  @doc """
  Disconnects existing sockets for the given tokens.
  """
  def disconnect_sessions(tokens) do
    Enum.each(tokens, fn %{token: token} ->
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(user_session_topic(token), "disconnect", %{})
    end)
  end

  defp user_session_topic(token), do: "users_sessions:#{Base.url_encode64(token)}"

  @doc """
  Handles mounting and authenticating the current_scope in LiveViews.

  ## `on_mount` arguments

    * `:mount_current_scope` - Assigns current_scope
      to socket assigns based on user_token, or nil if
      there's no user_token or no matching user.

    * `:require_authenticated` - Authenticates the user from the session,
      and assigns the current_scope to socket assigns based
      on user_token.
      Redirects to login page if there's no logged user.

  ## Examples

  Use the `on_mount` lifecycle macro in LiveViews to mount or authenticate
  the `current_scope`:

      defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PageLive do
        use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

        on_mount {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}
        ...
      end

  Or use the `live_session` of your router to invoke the on_mount callback:

      live_session :authenticated, on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
        live "/profile", ProfileLive, :index
      end
  """
  def on_mount(:mount_current_scope, _params, session, socket) do
    {:cont, mount_current_scope(socket, session)}
  end

  def on_mount(:require_authenticated, _params, session, socket) do
    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)

    if socket.assigns.current_scope && socket.assigns.current_scope.user do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must log in to access this page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  def on_mount(:require_sudo_mode, _params, session, socket) do
    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)

    if Users.sudo_mode?(socket.assigns.current_scope.user, -10) do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must re-authenticate to access this page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  defp mount_current_scope(socket, session) do
    Phoenix.Component.assign_new(socket, :current_scope, fn ->
      {user, _} =
        if user_token = session["user_token"] do
          Users.get_user_by_session_token(user_token)
        end || {nil, nil}

      scope_with_active_account(user)
    end)
  end

  # There's no persisted "current account" selection yet (the account
  # picker doesn't write one anywhere), so every account-scoped page
  # would otherwise see a permanently nil `active_account_id`. Until
  # that selection is persisted, default a signed-in user onto one of
  # their accounts — the common case is a single-account owner, for
  # whom this is unambiguous.
  defp scope_with_active_account(nil), do: Scope.for_user(nil)

  defp scope_with_active_account(user) do
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.list_accounts(scope) do
      [account | _] -> %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
      [] -> scope
    end
  end

  @doc "Returns the path to redirect to after log in."
  # the user was already logged in, redirect to settings
  def signed_in_path(%Plug.Conn{assigns: %{current_scope: %Scope{user: %Users.User{}}}}) do
    ~p"/users/settings"
  end

  def signed_in_path(_), do: ~p"/"

  @doc """
  Plug for routes that require the user to be authenticated.
  """
  def require_authenticated_user(conn, _opts) do
    if conn.assigns.current_scope && conn.assigns.current_scope.user do
      conn
    else
      conn
      |> put_flash(:error, "You must log in to access this page.")
      |> maybe_store_return_to()
      |> redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")
      |> halt()
    end
  end

  defp maybe_store_return_to(%{method: "GET"} = conn) do
    put_session(conn, :user_return_to, current_path(conn))
  end

  defp maybe_store_return_to(conn), do: conn
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.Scope do
  @moduledoc """
  Defines the scope of the caller to be used throughout the app.

  The `CleanerCrm.Users.Scope` allows public interfaces to receive
  information about the caller, such as if the call is initiated from an
  end-user, and if so, which user. Additionally, such a scope can carry fields
  such as "super user" or other privileges for use in authorization checks,
  or to ensure specific code paths can only be accessed for a given scope.

  It is useful for logging as well as for scoping pubsub subscriptions and
  broadcasts when a caller subscribes to an interface or performs a particular
  action.

  Feel free to extend the fields on this struct to fit the needs of
  growing application requirements.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  defstruct user: nil,
            active_account: nil,
            active_account_id: nil

  @doc """
  Creates a scope for the given user.

  Returns nil if no user is given.
  """
  def for_user(%User{} = user) do
    %__MODULE__{user: user}
  end

  def for_user(nil), do: nil
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Authorization do
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def authorize(action, %Scope{} = scope, resource) do
    case {action, resource} do
      {:read_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(scope.user.id, account_id)

      {:manage_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        user_role = MembersRepository.get_user_role(scope.user.id, account_id)
        user_role in [:owner, :admin]

      {:manage_members, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        user_role = MembersRepository.get_user_role(scope.user.id, account_id)
        user_role in [:owner, :admin]

      {:delete_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        user_role = MembersRepository.get_user_role(scope.user.id, account_id)
        user_role == :owner

      _ ->
        false
    end
  end

  def authorize!(action, scope, resource) do
    unless authorize(action, scope, resource) do
      raise "Unauthorized: #{action} on #{inspect(resource)}"
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.TimesheetExportController do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking

  def show(conn, %{"start_date" => start_date, "end_date" => end_date}) do
    period = {Date.from_iso8601!(start_date), Date.from_iso8601!(end_date)}

    case TimeTracking.export_pay_period_csv(conn.assigns.current_scope, period) do
      {:ok, csv} ->
        conn
        |> put_resp_content_type("text/csv")
        |> put_resp_header(
          "content-disposition",
          ~s(attachment; filename="payroll-#{start_date}-#{end_date}.csv")
        )
        |> send_resp(200, csv)

      {:error, :unresolved_entries} ->
        conn
        |> put_flash(:error, "Resolve the unresolved time entry before exporting")
        |> redirect(to: ~p"/timesheets")
    end
  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story840.Criterion7193Spex do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Story 840 — See an audit trail of schedule and record changes
4	  Criterion 7193 — Office staff reschedules a job and it is logged: an
5	  audit entry records who moved the job, the old and new times, and
6	  the timestamp of the change.
7	
8	  Assumes `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent` (per the
9	  project's architecture spec, opened from the board at `/schedule`)
10	  exposes a `[data-test='job-<id>-edit-button']` trigger and a
11	  `[data-test='job-form']` submitted via `render_submit` with
12	  `scheduled_date`/`start_time`/`end_time` fields. Assumes
13	  `CleanerCrmWeb.AuditLive` (`/audit`) renders a
14	  `[data-test='audit-entries']` list where each entry shows its actor,
15	  action, one `"<Field label>: <old> → <new>"` line per changed field,
16	  and today's date as its timestamp.
17	  """
18	
19	  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case
20	
21	  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures
22	
23	  spex "office staff reschedules a job and it is logged" do
24	    scenario "moving a job from Tuesday 9:00 to Wednesday 1:00 pm is recorded" do
25	      given_ "office staffer Dana is logged in with an active account", context do
26	        user =
27	          Fixtures.user_fixture(%{
28	            email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
29	          })
30	
31	        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
32	        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
33	        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)
34	
35	        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
36	      end
37	
38	      given_ "a job is scheduled for Tuesday at 9:00 am", context do
39	        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Tuesday client"})
40	
41	        job =
42	          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
43	            scheduled_date: tuesday(),
44	            start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
45	            end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
46	          })
47	
48	        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job})}
49	      end
50	
51	      when_ "Dana moves the job to Wednesday at 1:00 pm", context do
52	        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story840.Criterion7193Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 840 — See an audit trail of schedule and record changes
  Criterion 7193 — Office staff reschedules a job and it is logged: an
  audit entry records who moved the job, the old and new times, and
  the timestamp of the change.

  Assumes `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent` (per the
  project's architecture spec, opened from the board at `/schedule`)
  exposes a `[data-test='job-<id>-edit-button']` trigger and a
  `[data-test='job-form']` submitted via `render_submit` with
  `scheduled_date`/`start_time`/`end_time` fields. Assumes
  `CleanerCrmWeb.AuditLive` (`/audit`) renders a
  `[data-test='audit-entries']` list where each entry shows its actor,
  action, one `"<Field label>: <old> → <new>"` line per changed field,
  and today's date as its timestamp.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "office staff reschedules a job and it is logged" do
    scenario "moving a job from Tuesday 9:00 to Wednesday 1:00 pm is recorded" do
      given_ "office staffer Dana is logged in with an active account", context do
        user =
          Fixtures.user_fixture(%{
            email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a job is scheduled for Tuesday at 9:00 am", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Tuesday client"})

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            scheduled_date: tuesday(),
            start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "Dana moves the job to Wednesday at 1:00 pm", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        board_live
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-edit-button']")
        |> render_click()

        board_live
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{
            scheduled_date: Date.to_iso8601(wednesday()),
            start_time: "13:00",
            end_time: "15:00"
          }
        )
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :board_live, board_live)}
      end

      then_ "an audit entry names Dana as the one who rescheduled the job", context do
        {:ok, _audit_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/audit")

        assert html =~ context.user.email
        assert html =~ "rescheduled"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the audit entry records the old and new times and the timestamp of the change",
            context do
        {:ok, _audit_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/audit")

        assert html =~
                 "Scheduled date: #{Date.to_iso8601(tuesday())} → #{Date.to_iso8601(wednesday())}"

        assert html =~ "Start time: 09:00:00 → 13:00:00"
        assert html =~ Date.to_iso8601(Date.utc_today())

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp tuesday do
    monday = week_monday()
    Date.add(monday, 1)
  end

  defp wednesday do
    monday = week_monday()
    Date.add(monday, 2)
  end

  defp week_monday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    Date.add(today, -(Date.day_of_week(today) - 1))
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository do
  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, Member}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  def add_user_to_account(user_id, account_id, role \\ :member) do
    %Member{}
    |> Member.changeset(%{user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id, role: role})
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def remove_user_from_account(user_id, account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Member, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_found}

      member ->
        case member.role do
          :owner ->
            owner_count = count_owners(account_id)
            if owner_count > 1, do: Repo.delete(member), else: {:error, :last_owner}

          _ ->
            Repo.delete(member)
        end
    end
  end

  def update_user_role(user_id, account_id, role) do
    case Repo.get_by(Member, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_found}

      member ->
        changeset = Member.update_role_changeset(member, %{role: role})
        validated_changeset = Member.validate_owner_exists(changeset, Repo)

        case validated_changeset.valid? do
          true -> Repo.update(validated_changeset)
          false -> {:error, validated_changeset}
        end
    end
  end

  def get_user_role(user_id, account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Member, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> nil
      member -> member.role
    end
  end

  def user_has_account_access?(user_id, account_id) do
    Repo.exists?(from m in Member, where: m.user_id == ^user_id and m.account_id == ^account_id)
  end

  def can_add_user_to_account?(_account_id), do: true

  def count_account_users(account_id) do
    Repo.aggregate(from(m in Member, where: m.account_id == ^account_id), :count)
  end

  def list_user_accounts(user_id) do
    from(a in Account,
      join: m in Member,
      on: m.account_id == a.id,
      where: m.user_id == ^user_id
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def list_account_users(account_id) do
    from(u in User,
      join: m in Member,
      on: m.user_id == u.id,
      where: m.account_id == ^account_id
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def list_account_members(account_id) do
    from(m in Member,
      where: m.account_id == ^account_id,
      preload: [:user]
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def list_accounts_with_role(user_id, role) do
    from(a in Account,
      join: m in Member,
      on: m.account_id == a.id,
      where: m.user_id == ^user_id and m.role == ^role
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def by_user(user_id), do: from(m in Member, where: m.user_id == ^user_id)
  def by_account(account_id), do: from(m in Member, where: m.account_id == ^account_id)
  def by_role(role), do: from(m in Member, where: m.role == ^role)
  def with_user_preloads, do: from(m in Member, preload: [:user])
  def with_account_preloads, do: from(m in Member, preload: [:account])

  defp count_owners(account_id) do
    Repo.aggregate(
      from(m in Member, where: m.account_id == ^account_id and m.role == :owner),
      :count
    )
  end
end

# QA seed script — idempotent. Run with: mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs
#
# Creates two confirmed users with passwords (an owner and a cleaner) and
# one account (the cleaning company) owned by the owner. Prints credentials.

alias CleanerCrm.{Users, Accounts}
alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

qa_password = "qa password 1234"

ensure_user = fn email ->
  case Users.get_user_by_email(email) do
    nil ->
      {:ok, user} = Users.register_user(%{email: email})

      # Confirm via the magic-link flow (same path a real user takes).
      {:ok, email_struct} = Users.deliver_login_instructions(user, &"[TOKEN]#{&1}[TOKEN]")
      [_, token | _] = String.split(email_struct.text_body, "[TOKEN]")
      {:ok, {user, _expired}} = Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token)

      {:ok, {user, _expired}} = Users.update_user_password(user, %{password: qa_password})
      user

    user ->
      user
  end
end

owner = ensure_user.("qa-owner@cleanercrm.test")
cleaner = ensure_user.("qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test")

owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)

account =
  case Accounts.list_accounts(owner_scope) do
    [account | _] ->
      account

    [] ->
      {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(owner_scope, %{name: "QA Sparkle Cleaning Co"})
      account
  end

IO.puts("""

QA seed complete.

  Owner:   qa-owner@cleanercrm.test / #{qa_password}
  Cleaner: qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test / #{qa_password}
  Account: #{account.name} (id: #{account.id})

  Log in at: http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in
""")

# Story 834 QA seed script — idempotent. Run with:
#   mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds_834.exs
#
# Builds on priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs (owner + cleaner + account must already
# exist). Adds cleaners and jobs covering all 5 acceptance criteria for
# "Dispatch from a single weekly schedule board":
#   - 4 cleaners each with a job Mon-Thu this week (whole-week-at-a-glance)
#   - Ben also has a Wed 10am-12pm job (conflict target)
#   - Ana has a Wed 1-3pm job (reassign-to-Ben target, no conflict)
#   - Ana has a Wed 11am-12pm job (conflict source — overlaps Ben's 10-12)
#   - An unassigned Thu 2-4pm job (dispatch target)
#
# Ben is a real password-login user (not a placeholder) so criterion 7177
# can be verified by actually logging in as Ben in the browser.

alias CleanerCrm.{Users, Accounts, Clients, Scheduling}
alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

qa_password = "qa password 1234"

owner = Users.get_user_by_email("qa-owner@cleanercrm.test") || raise "run qa_seeds.exs first"
owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)
[account | _] = Accounts.list_accounts(owner_scope)
scope = %{owner_scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}

ensure_login_user = fn email ->
  case Users.get_user_by_email(email) do
    nil ->
      {:ok, user} = Users.register_user(%{email: email})
      {:ok, email_struct} = Users.deliver_login_instructions(user, &"[TOKEN]#{&1}[TOKEN]")
      [_, token | _] = String.split(email_struct.text_body, "[TOKEN]")
      {:ok, {user, _}} = Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token)
      {:ok, {user, _}} = Users.update_user_password(user, %{password: qa_password})
      user

    user ->
      user
  end
end

ensure_member = fn user ->
  already_member? =
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account.id)
    |> Enum.any?(&(&1.user_id == user.id))

  unless already_member? do
    {:ok, _member} = Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
  end
end

ensure_cleaner = fn name ->
  case Scheduling.list_cleaners(scope) |> Enum.find(&(&1.name == name)) do
    nil ->
      {:ok, cleaner} = Scheduling.register_cleaner(scope, name)
      cleaner

    cleaner ->
      cleaner
  end
end

ensure_client = fn name ->
  case Clients.list_clients(scope) |> Enum.find(&(&1.name == name)) do
    nil ->
      {:ok, client} = Clients.create_client(scope, %{name: name})
      client

    client ->
      client
  end
end

ensure_job = fn attrs ->
  scheduled_date = Map.fetch!(attrs, :scheduled_date)
  start_time = Map.fetch!(attrs, :start_time)

  existing =
    scope
    |> Scheduling.list_jobs()
    |> Enum.find(&(&1.scheduled_date == scheduled_date and &1.start_time == start_time and
                     &1.client_id == attrs[:client_id]))

  case existing do
    nil ->
      {:ok, job} = Scheduling.create_job(scope, attrs)
      job

    job ->
      job
  end
end

today = Date.utc_today()
monday = Date.add(today, -(Date.day_of_week(today) - 1))
wednesday = Date.add(monday, 2)
thursday = Date.add(monday, 3)

ben = ensure_login_user.("qa-ben-834@cleanercrm.test")
ensure_member.(ben)

ana = ensure_cleaner.("Ana QA834")
chloe = ensure_cleaner.("Chloe QA834")
dana = ensure_cleaner.("Dana QA834")

client_a = ensure_client.("Story834 Client A")
client_b = ensure_client.("Story834 Client B")
client_c = ensure_client.("Story834 Client C")
client_d = ensure_client.("Story834 Client D")
client_e = ensure_client.("Story834 Client E")
client_unassigned = ensure_client.("Story834 Client Unassigned")

# Whole-week-at-a-glance: one job per cleaner, Mon-Thu
mon_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_a.id,
    cleaner_id: ana.id,
    scheduled_date: monday,
    start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("100.00")
  })

tue_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_b.id,
    cleaner_id: ben.id,
    scheduled_date: Date.add(monday, 1),
    start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("100.00")
  })

wed_job_chloe =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_c.id,
    cleaner_id: chloe.id,
    scheduled_date: wednesday,
    start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("100.00")
  })

thu_job_dana =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_d.id,
    cleaner_id: dana.id,
    scheduled_date: thursday,
    start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("100.00")
  })

# Reassign target: Ana's Wed 1-3pm job -> will be moved to Ben in-browser
reassign_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_e.id,
    cleaner_id: ana.id,
    scheduled_date: wednesday,
    start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[15:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("120.00")
  })

# Conflict setup: Ben already has Wed 10am-12pm
ben_conflict_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_b.id,
    cleaner_id: ben.id,
    scheduled_date: wednesday,
    start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[12:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("100.00")
  })

# Conflict source: Ana's Wed 11am-12pm job -> attempting to move onto Ben must be rejected
conflict_source_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_a.id,
    cleaner_id: ana.id,
    scheduled_date: wednesday,
    start_time: ~T[11:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[12:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("80.00")
  })

# Dispatch target: unassigned Thu 2-4pm job
unassigned_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_unassigned.id,
    cleaner_id: nil,
    scheduled_date: thursday,
    start_time: ~T[14:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[16:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("90.00")
  })

IO.puts("""

Story 834 QA seed complete.

  Cleaners:
    Ana QA834:   id=#{ana.id}
    Ben:         id=#{ben.id}  login=qa-ben-834@cleanercrm.test / #{qa_password}
    Chloe QA834: id=#{chloe.id}
    Dana QA834:  id=#{dana.id}

  Jobs:
    Monday    (whole-week):        job-#{mon_job.id}    Ana
    Tuesday   (whole-week):        job-#{tue_job.id}    Ben
    Wednesday (whole-week):        job-#{wed_job_chloe.id}    Chloe
    Thursday  (whole-week):        job-#{thu_job_dana.id}    Dana
    Wednesday (reassign target):   job-#{reassign_job.id}    Ana 1-3pm -> move to Ben
    Wednesday (Ben's existing):    job-#{ben_conflict_job.id}    Ben 10am-12pm
    Wednesday (conflict source):   job-#{conflict_source_job.id}    Ana 11am-12pm -> moving to Ben must be BLOCKED
    Thursday  (unassigned):        job-#{unassigned_job.id}    unassigned 2-4pm -> assign to Chloe or Dana

  Week Monday: #{monday}
""")

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.QualityLive.Review do
  @moduledoc """
  Completed-job review with photos and checklist results, and the
  account's filed incident reports.

  ## Routes

    * `/quality` (`:index`) — every job (for picking one to review) and
      the account's incident reports, newest first, as the office's
      notification feed.
    * `/quality/:job_id` (`:show`) — one job's checklist, its
      timestamped before/after photos as proof of work, and the
      owner's quality rating.

  ## Dependencies

  - `CleanerCrm.Quality`
  - `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` (read-only: job lookups)
  """

1	defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story834.Criterion7177Spex do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Story 834 — Dispatch from a single weekly schedule board
4	  Criterion 7177 — A job reassigned on the board is reflected on the
5	  newly assigned cleaner's own schedule.
6	
7	  Story 834's only linked surface is `ScheduleLive.Board`; the
8	  cleaner-facing `FieldLive` (stories 841-845) is a day view, not a
9	  week view. "Ben views his own schedule for the week" is modeled here
10	  as Ben logging in and visiting the same `/schedule` board under his
11	  own session, proving the reassignment is durable server-side state
12	  rather than optimistic UI on the reassigning owner's LiveView.
13	  """
14	
15	  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case
16	
17	  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures
18	
19	  spex "reassignment reaches the newly assigned cleaner's schedule" do
20	    scenario "Ben sees the job that was moved from Ana, and Ana no longer does" do
21	      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
22	        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
23	        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
24	        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
25	        scope = %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
26	        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)
27	
28	        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
29	      end
30	
31	      given_ "a job is reassigned from Ana to Ben on the board", context do
32	        ana =
33	          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
34	            email: "ana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
35	          })
36	
37	        ben =
38	          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
39	            email: "ben-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
40	          })
41	
42	        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Reassigned client"})
43	
44	        job =
45	          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
46	            cleaner_id: ana.id,
47	            scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
48	            start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
49	            end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
50	          })
51	
52	        {:ok, owner_view, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")
53	
54	        owner_view
55	        |> element("[data-test='job-#{job.id}-cleaner-select']")
56	        |> render_change(%{"cleaner_id" => to_string(ben.id)})
57	
58	        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{ana: ana, ben: ben, job: job})}
59	      end
60	
61	      when_ "Ben views his own schedule for the week", context do
62	        bens_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(build_conn(), context.ben)

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story834.Criterion7177Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 834 — Dispatch from a single weekly schedule board
  Criterion 7177 — A job reassigned on the board is reflected on the
  newly assigned cleaner's own schedule.

  Story 834's only linked surface is `ScheduleLive.Board`; the
  cleaner-facing `FieldLive` (stories 841-845) is a day view, not a
  week view. "Ben views his own schedule for the week" is modeled here
  as Ben logging in and visiting the same `/schedule` board under his
  own session, proving the reassignment is durable server-side state
  rather than optimistic UI on the reassigning owner's LiveView.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "reassignment reaches the newly assigned cleaner's schedule" do
    scenario "Ben sees the job that was moved from Ana, and Ana no longer does" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        scope = %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a job is reassigned from Ana to Ben on the board", context do
        ana =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "ana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        ben =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "ben-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Reassigned client"})

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: ana.id,
            scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
            start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
          })

        {:ok, owner_view, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        owner_view
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{job.id}-cleaner-select']")
        |> render_change(%{"cleaner_id" => to_string(ben.id)})

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{ana: ana, ben: ben, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "Ben views his own schedule for the week", context do
        bens_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(build_conn(), context.ben)
        {:ok, bens_view, _html} = live(bens_conn, ~p"/schedule")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :bens_view, bens_view)}
      end

      then_ "the reassigned job appears on Ben's schedule", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.bens_view,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{context.ben.id}'] [data-test='job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "it is gone from Ana's schedule", context do
        refute has_element?(
                 context.bens_view,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{context.ana.id}'] [data-test='job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story834.Criterion7177Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 834 — Dispatch from a single weekly schedule board
  Criterion 7177 — A job reassigned on the board is reflected on the
  newly assigned cleaner's own schedule.

  Story 834's only linked surface is `ScheduleLive.Board`; the
  cleaner-facing `FieldLive` (stories 841-845) is a day view, not a
  week view. "Ben views his own schedule for the week" is modeled here
  as Ben logging in and visiting the same `/schedule` board under his
  own session, proving the reassignment is durable server-side state
  rather than optimistic UI on the reassigning owner's LiveView.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "reassignment reaches the newly assigned cleaner's schedule" do
    scenario "Ben sees the job that was moved from Ana, and Ana no longer does" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        scope = %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a job is reassigned from Ana to Ben on the board", context do
        ana =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "ana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        ben =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "ben-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Reassigned client"})

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: ana.id,
            scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
            start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
          })

        {:ok, owner_view, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        owner_view
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{job.id}-cleaner-select']")
        |> render_change(%{"cleaner_id" => to_string(ben.id)})

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{ana: ana, ben: ben, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "Ben views his own schedule for the week", context do
        bens_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(build_conn(), context.ben)
        {:ok, bens_view, _html} = live(bens_conn, ~p"/schedule")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :bens_view, bens_view)}
      end

      then_ "the reassigned job appears on Ben's schedule", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.bens_view,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{context.ben.id}'] [data-test='job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "it is gone from Ana's schedule", context do
        refute has_element?(
                 context.bens_view,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{context.ana.id}'] [data-test='job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole do
  @moduledoc """
  Restricts office-only LiveViews — scheduling, timesheets, quality,
  invoices, clients, quotes, reminders, and the audit trail — to
  account owners and admins.

  A cleaner (or anyone with no office role on the active account) is
  redirected to `/field`, their own surface, with an error flash.
  Must run after `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth`'s `:require_authenticated`
  on_mount in the same `live_session`, since it relies on
  `current_scope.user` already being assigned.

  ## Usage

      live_session :require_office_role,
        on_mount: [
          {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
          {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
        ] do
        live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
        ...
      end
  """

  import Phoenix.LiveView
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts

  def on_mount(:default, _params, _session, socket) do
    scope = socket.assigns.current_scope

    if office_role?(scope) do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> put_flash(:error, "You don't have access to that page.")
        |> redirect(to: ~p"/field")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  defp office_role?(%{active_account_id: nil}), do: false

  defp office_role?(scope),

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do

      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show

      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index

      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their

    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index

      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their
    # reminder — no login, so `:browser` (not `:require_authenticated_user`)
    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end
end
